description: Chat with coding agents over the Agent Client Protocol, install agents from the ACP Registry
config.language: Language of the Code ACP interface.
config.language.auto: Same as the VS Code display language
config.customAgents: ACP agents run from local commands, by name. They appear in the chat's agent picker next to the installed agents; their env is added on top of codeAcp.env.
config.env: Extra environment variables for the agent (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
config.nodePath: Node used to run agents installed via npm.
config.ccusagePath: Path of the ccusage executable for the Usage page (e.g. a global install). Empty runs a pinned release through npx.
config.followAgent: Open the files the agent reads and edits in the editor, at the line it is working on, and briefly highlight the lines it changes.
config.autoScroll: Keep the chat scrolled to the newest content while the agent replies. Turn off to stay where you scrolled.
config.showChanges: Show the bar above the message box that lists the files the agent changed, with Undo all and Keep all, and Keep and Undo above each change in the editor.
config.showRestore: Show the Restore button on your messages, which puts the files the agent changed back to how they were before that message.
config.tracing: For advanced users. Shows each turn's stop reason, duration, tokens, cost and context in the chat, and logs every ACP message in the Code ACP Trace output channel. The log can contain file contents, tool input and output: env and header values and fields named like secrets are masked, but other secrets may remain, and VS Code keeps output channels in its log folder.
config.checkAgentUpdates: Check the ACP Registry for agent updates on startup and offer to install them.
command.cancelCommitMessage: Code ACP: Stop Generating Commit Message
command.addSelection: Code ACP: Add Selection to Chat
command.addTerminalSelection: Code ACP: Add Terminal Selection to Chat
command.addTerminalOutput: Code ACP: Add Last Command Output to Chat
command.addTerminalFailure: Code ACP: Add Last Failed Command to Chat
config.worktreeForNewTabs: Tick the Worktree box of each new chat: its first message creates a git worktree of its own, on a new branch, so chats don't touch each other's files or your local checkout. Folders outside git are not affected.
config.worktreeCopyFiles: Ignored files to copy from your checkout into each new worktree, as gitignore patterns relative to the repository, such as .env or node_modules. Files git doesn't ignore are never copied.
config.worktreeSetupCommand: Shell command to run at the top of each new worktree, such as npm install. The agent starts once it finishes. It is read from user settings only, so a repository can't set it.
config.worktreeProjectSetupCommand: This project's shell command to run at the top of each new worktree, instead of the setup command in your user settings. It is read from workspace or folder settings only. Code ACP asks before running it, and asks again when the command or a file it names changes.
config.allowedHttpHosts: Hosts that links from agents may open over plain http, besides localhost and 127.0.0.1, which are always allowed. Names or IP addresses, without a port. Anyone on the network can read what is sent over http.
config.autoApprove: Which agent requests are answered without asking you. Everything else still asks. Agents describe their own tools, so these rules save clicks but are no security boundary. Each workspace can change them from the Permissions page of Code ACP's settings.
config.autoApprove.read: Reading and searching files inside the chat's folder, including secrets stored there.
config.autoApprove.edit: Editing and moving files inside the chat's folder, except .git and .vscode. Files elsewhere can still run later, such as package.json scripts or agent configuration.
config.autoApprove.execute: Running any command, anywhere on this machine.
config.autoApprove.fetch: Accessing any network address. Together with reading files, this lets an agent send your secrets out without asking.
config.autoApprove.worktreeTabs: In chats with a worktree of their own: everything that says what it does, including deletes and paths outside the worktree. A worktree is no sandbox.
config.mcpServers: Extra MCP servers passed to every agent session, on top of the agent's own MCP config. Keyed by server name, in the `.mcp.json` shape: `{ "command": "npx", "args": [...], "env": {...} }` for stdio, or `{ "type": "http" | "sse", "url": "...", "headers": {...} }`. Changes apply to new or reopened sessions.
config.commitMessage.agent: Id of the installed agent that generates commit messages. Empty: the default agent.
config.commitMessage.model: Model for generating commit messages (its id or name, as the agent lists it). Empty: the agent's default model.
config.commitMessage.effort: Effort (level of thinking) for generating commit messages, as the agent lists it. Empty: the agent's default. "lowest": the least the agent offers.
config.commitMessage.fastMode: Turn the agent's fast mode on or off for generating commit messages. "default": leave it as the agent has it.
config.commitMessage.instructions: Extra instructions for generating commit messages, e.g. a convention such as Conventional Commits.
capabilities.virtualWorkspaces: Agents run as processes that need the workspace folders on disk.
command.addProblems: Code ACP: Add File Problems to Chat
command.addWorkspaceProblems: Code ACP: Add Workspace Problems to Chat
config.rememberSessionOptions: Start and reopen chats with the model, effort and fast mode you last picked for the agent, except where codeAcp.sessionDefaults sets them.
config.sessionDefaults: The model, effort and fast mode to start chats with, by agent id. These win over the last picked; what is left out follows codeAcp.rememberSessionOptions.
config.notifications: Notify when a conversation you aren't looking at finishes or needs your approval. The chat view's badge counts them either way.
config.notifyFinished: Also notify when a conversation you aren't looking at finishes. Approval requests and questions from the agent still notify. Has no effect while codeAcp.notifications is off.
command.showAttention: Code ACP: Show Conversation That Needs You
walkthrough.title: Get started with Code ACP
walkthrough.description: Install a coding agent, check your machine and start chatting.
walkthrough.install.title: Install an agent
walkthrough.install.description:
Code ACP talks to coding agents over the Agent Client Protocol. Install one from the ACP Registry, such as Claude, Codex or OpenCode. You can also add your own from a local command in Settings.
[Manage Agents](command:codeAcp.manageAgents)
walkthrough.install.alt: A grid of agents, one of them being installed.
walkthrough.doctor.title: Check your setup
walkthrough.doctor.description:
Agents installed with npm need Node.js, uvx agents need uv, and worktrees need git. Doctor checks these, starts each agent and tells you which ones need a login. It only starts them and sends no prompts.
[Run Doctor](command:codeAcp.doctor)
walkthrough.doctor.alt: A checklist with one row needing attention.
walkthrough.chat.title: Open the chat
walkthrough.chat.description:
The chat lives in the secondary side bar. Open it with Ctrl+Alt+A (Cmd+Alt+A on macOS). If the agent asks you to sign in, use the Log in button there.
[Open Chat](command:codeAcp.chat.focus)
walkthrough.chat.alt: An editor with the chat in the side bar next to it.
walkthrough.parallel.title: Work in parallel
walkthrough.parallel.description:
Run a chat in a git worktree of its own, or tick Compare in the composer to send one prompt to several agents and apply the best result. Choose what agents may do without asking on the Permissions page of Settings.
[Open Settings](command:codeAcp.openSettings)
walkthrough.parallel.alt: Three branches leaving one commit, the best of them marked.
